title: Sell Mineral Rights in Hunker, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Hunker, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Hunker in Westmoreland County? Learn what wet-gas Marcellus interests are worth here and how a fair, no-pressure offer works.
heroLead: Hunker is a small crossroads community in Sewickley Township, sitting inside one of the wettest, richest parts of the Marcellus fairway in Westmoreland County.
intro: My grandfather signed his first gas lease on a farm not far from Hunker back when a landman still drove out in person and shook your hand at the kitchen table. Sixty years later his grandkids inherited an eighth of the minerals under that same ground, split four ways, and none of us had any idea what it was worth or who to call. That's the situation a lot of Hunker families are sitting in right now — small unincorporated place, big Marcellus wet-gas numbers underneath it, and a deed that hasn't been touched since a great-aunt passed it down.

sections.heading: Why Hunker Sits in a Premium Part of the Play
paragraphs: Westmoreland County is inside the wet-gas window of the Marcellus, which means the gas coming up here carries natural gas liquids — ethane, propane, butane — alongside the methane. Operators pay more attention to wet-gas acreage than dry-gas acreage because there's a second revenue stream at the processing plant, and that has kept horizontal development active around Sewickley Township for years even when prices dipped elsewhere in the state.

sections.heading: What Your Deed Probably Says
paragraphs: Most of the older Hunker-area deeds we look at reserved minerals in fractions — a half, a third, sometimes a sixteenth — going back to a farm sale in the early-to-mid 1900s. If your name isn't the only one on the royalty statement, or if the statement lists an old family surname instead of yours, you're probably holding an inherited fractional interest that never went through a formal transfer. That's normal, and it's fixable at the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg with the right paperwork.

sections.heading: The Post-Production Deduction Problem
paragraphs: This is the part that makes people angry, and rightfully so. Pennsylvania operators are allowed to subtract gathering, compression, and processing costs from your royalty before they cut the check, under the standard set by the Kilmer v. Elexco decision — unless your lease specifically forbids it. Combined with the state's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act, which only guarantees you a floor of one-eighth, plenty of Hunker landowners open a royalty statement and find a number far smaller than what the wellhead price would suggest. We read that statement line by line before we ever talk numbers with you.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer to sell mineral rights near Hunker?
faqs.answer: You don't need one to get a conversation started, but for anything with fractional or inherited ownership we'd rather you have a title attorney review the offer before you sign — we'll tell you that upfront, not after.

faqs.question: Is my interest too small to be worth selling?
faqs.answer: Small fractional interests around Hunker come up constantly given how many farms were split among heirs. Size affects the number, not whether we'll look at it.

faqs.question: How is the value figured for gas that hasn't been drilled yet?
faqs.answer: It depends on nearby lease activity, unit formation filed with the county, and current royalty checks if a well is already producing — we walk through those factors with you rather than throwing out a figure with nothing behind it.
